Poll and reconcile the hosted Session before saving the resulting local state; a deadline failure preserves recovery evidence.

journeys.name: Inspect a Session
journeys.summary: ocbox status shows one Session; for a Session with a Sandbox the provider is asked for its live state.

steps.story: `ocbox status [session]` loads opencloudbox.toml and this folder's lifecycle file. With no Session selected it fails with ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND "run ocbox start or ocbox use"; an unknown id fails with the same code.

For a Session that is not destroyed and has a Sandbox, the provider is asked for the live Sandbox (getSession for the hosted provider) and that replaces the stored copy. If the mapping is unavailable for this login, API or project it fails with SANDBOX_NOT_FOUND.
Human output is one line: * for the selected Session, id, state, provider state, raw state and any running operation. --json keeps the full view.

journeys.name: List local Sessions
journeys.summary: ocbox ls prints the Sessions recorded for this folder, from the lifecycle file only.

steps.story: Load opencloudbox.toml and the lifecycle file for this folder; a missing config gives CONFIG_INVALID. Session views resolve provider capabilities locally; ls does not call listSessions or observe remote sandbox state.

Sort recorded Sessions by creation time and construct each view from stored primary bindings and current-operation records. Resolve provider capabilities locally; this does not refresh hosted Session state.
Human output marks the selected Session with * and shows local Session/provider state, or No Sessions for an empty file. --json/--jsonl emit the structured views through the redacting output writer.

journeys.name: Select a Session
journeys.summary: ocbox use makes an existing Session the one later commands act on.

steps.story: `ocbox use <session>` requires a UUID or ULID id, loads opencloudbox.toml and builds the lifecycle service for this folder.
Under the lifecycle file lock the active Session id is replaced. An id that is not in the file fails with ENVIRONMENT_NOT_FOUND and nothing changes; the Session is not contacted at the provider.
The updated Session is printed as one line (id, state, provider state); --json keeps the full view.

journeys.name: Inspect source differences
journeys.summary: ocbox sync diff shows what a push or pull would change, without writing anything (fake provider only).

steps.story: diff resolves the selected Session, the local folder and the remote workspace. For the hosted ocbox provider it stops with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED "sync diff is not supported for hosted sandboxes yet".

It refuses while a transfer journal or pending baseline needs recovery, then scans both sides: built-in exclusions first, then .gitignore, .opencloudboxignore and --exclude/--include. Paths that collide or are unsafe are reported as blocked.

planSync compares local, remote and the last verified baseline into additions, modifications, deletions, renames and conflicts. With no baseline, files on both sides give a first-sync conflict. Nothing is written and the baseline state is unchanged.

journeys.name: Recover an interrupted local sync
journeys.summary: ocbox sync recover resolves a transfer journal left by a crashed push or pull and reconciles the pending baseline.

steps.story: recover is local-only: for the hosted ocbox provider it stops with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED. Otherwise it resolves the Session and takes the per-Session sync lock (5 s wait, then OPERATION_CONFLICT).

It checks the remote and the local target for a journal and recovers each one that needs it. Recovery restores the original target (or its absence) and never promotes staged content; an ambiguous journal with both target and backup fails with the RECOVERY_REQUIRED error.
A pending baseline is then promoted if the target matches its snapshot hash, otherwise discarded and the old baseline kept. The result says whether anything was recovered and the Operation id.

journeys.name: Cancel a command
journeys.summary: Cancel a running command from another terminal and wait for a terminal result.

steps.story: Resolve the last execution or explicit ID and --sandbox in local lifecycle state; --wait-timeout defaults to 30000 ms and Ctrl-C cancels this wait. Missing work is a typed error.
Read getExecution and verify its Session/Sandbox binding before cancellation. A terminal state clears the saved last execution and is returned immediately.
Request cancelExecution once (409 is tolerated), then observe until completed, failed or cancelled. Deadline/cancellation reports incomplete convergence instead of claiming the command stopped.

journeys.name: Install a coding-agent adapter
journeys.summary: ocbox agent setup <codex|claude-code> installs the owned routing hook; see the per-adapter journeys for the file-level steps.

steps.story: The adapter is a required argument (codex or claude-code; anything else is rejected). Flags owned by the other adapter, such as --layer with claude-code, are ignored with a warning only when the user typed them.

Both adapters plan before writing and refuse an unsupported version, a managed hook lock or an unrecognised hooks table. Claude Code setup writes straight away; Codex prints the plan and writes only with --yes (exit 2 when the plan is blocked).
An ownership manifest and backups let doctor and remove identify only this adapter's entries; a partial write fails and rolls back from the saved content.

journeys.name: Inspect adapter drift
journeys.summary: ocbox agent doctor reports whether the installed hook is healthy and what the adapter does and does not cover; it writes nothing.

steps.story: Doctor runs `claude --version` or `codex --version` and compares it with the pinned version (Claude Code 2.0.51, Codex 0.153.4).

It reads settings, policy sources and the ownership manifest and runs the checks: owned entries, manifest, drift, Session, routing boundary, hook contract and recursion guard. A failed check carries a remediation; nothing is written.
The result lists what is covered (Bash through the hook) and what stays local. Claude Code doctor sets exit code 1 when a check fails; Codex doctor throws when any check has status fail.

journeys.name: Remove owned adapter settings
journeys.summary: ocbox agent remove takes out only the entries the adapter owns and keeps everything the user added.

steps.story: Removal starts from the ownership grammar, not the manifest alone: only the exact `ocbox agent hook …` hook and the allow rule Bash(ocbox exec:*) (Claude Code) or exact owned hook groups (Codex) count as owned.

Codex removal applies only with --yes; without it the plan prints. Claude Code removal applies at once: it restores the backup byte for byte if the file still matches the recorded hashes, deletes a file setup created, otherwise rewrites the pruned document.
A container the user replaced with another type is reported as container-invalid with repair steps (status not-installed) and left untouched; the manifest is kept for repair, otherwise it is deleted.

journeys.name: Manage project metadata
journeys.summary: Choose one project CRUD action; the following request steps are alternatives, not a batch. Commands need hosted login but no selected Session.

steps.story: Build an issuer-bound metadata client; validate names (1–200), nonempty IDs and optional page limit (1–100). SIGINT supplies AbortSignal and the listener is disposed after completion.
project list: request one page with optional cursor/limit; the caller requests nextCursor explicitly.
project create: post the name with a supplied idempotency key or new UUID; require HTTP 201.
project get: request the supplied hosted ID without mutating selection. Require HTTP 200 or report a typed error.
project update: patch the required name with a supplied key or UUID; require HTTP 200.

Validate the successful resource/page shape, retaining request-id and replay metadata. Human output prints id/name lines and nextCursor; malformed responses fail INTERNAL without exposing response bodies.

journeys.name: Manage environment metadata
journeys.summary: Choose one environment CRUD action; the following request steps are alternatives, not a batch. Commands need hosted login but no selected Session.

steps.story: Build an issuer-bound metadata client; validate names (1–200), nonempty IDs and optional page limit (1–100). SIGINT supplies AbortSignal and the listener is disposed after completion.
environment list: request one page with optional cursor/limit; the caller requests nextCursor explicitly.
environment create: post the name with a supplied idempotency key or new UUID; require HTTP 201.
environment get: request the supplied hosted ID without mutating selection. Require HTTP 200 or report a typed error.
environment update: patch name and/or selected (at least one), with a stable supplied key or UUID; require HTTP 200.

Validate the successful resource/page shape, retaining request-id and replay metadata. Human output prints id/name lines and nextCursor; malformed responses fail INTERNAL without exposing response bodies.

journeys.name: Initialize project configuration
journeys.summary: ocbox init creates or validates opencloudbox.toml; with the hosted provider it also finds or creates the hosted project.

steps.story: `ocbox init [--provider fake|ocbox]` reads opencloudbox.toml or starts from the default config. The provider defaults to ocbox when logged in, else fake. An existing file is validated and only edited to add provider, project id or resource flags.
For ocbox without a project id it lists hosted projects page by page looking for one named like the folder; a repeated cursor aborts the loop with an error.
If none matches, a project with that name is created (201). The projectId is written to the file, which is created exclusively with mode 0600; a result of "created" or "validated" is printed.

journeys.name: Embedded public API capabilities
journeys.summary: Alternative public client/provider entry points, not one ordered request sequence. Normal CLI flows are separate; list/preview/operation-cancel ports are callable by embedding but have no CLI command.

steps.story: Alternative project list: request one page with cursor/limit (1–100), require 200 and validate ProjectPageSchema. CLI project list and init use this dispatch.
Alternative project create: validate a 1–200-character name, generate or retain the mutation key, require 201 and validate ProjectSchema.
Alternative project get: require a nonempty hosted project ID, require 200 and validate ProjectSchema without selecting a local Session.
Alternative project update: require hosted ID and name, send the mutation key, require 200 and validate ProjectSchema.
Alternative environment list: require project ID, request one cursor page with limit 1–100 and validate EnvironmentPageSchema after 200.
Alternative environment create: require project ID and a 1–200-character name, send a mutation key and validate EnvironmentSchema after 201.
Alternative environment get: require a hosted environment ID and validate EnvironmentSchema after 200; no local Session is needed.
Alternative environment update: require environment ID and at least name or selected, send a mutation key and validate EnvironmentSchema after 200.
During output collection, getExecution observes state when events are exhausted or repeated retryable event failures trigger fallback; invalid representations fail INTERNAL.
After terminal observation, validate getExecutionResult; retryable HTTP errors back off under the collection deadline, while other errors propagate.
Fetch event pages (default 100) by cursor, order and deduplicate sequence numbers; reset an invalid cursor and fall back after more than 3 consecutive retryable failures.
Poll getOperation with checkpointed attempts, state and progress until terminal success, failure or cancellation, under the default 5-minute loop deadline.
Embedded cancelHostedOperation reuses its mutation key, retries retryable HTTP errors for at most a 5-minute loop deadline and returns the validated cancel response. No CLI command calls this helper.
Hosted create verifies the configured project and sends only requested resources with a stable mutation key, then waits for both the Operation and running primary binding.
Embedded provider.list reads one hosted Session page and returns only owned primary bindings with existing local mappings. CLI ls uses the local lifecycle file instead. Require HTTP 200.
Provider get resolves the current login/project mapping and rejects a changed primary binding; a missing hosted Session marks the mapping stale rather than creating a replacement.
Destroy dispatches the stable mutation key, waits for its Operation, then confirms destroyed state/no primary binding or 404 before marking the mapping deleted.
Direct provider pause posts a mutation key and waits for paused state. Normal CLI pause refuses earlier because HOSTED_CAPABILITIES advertises supportsMemoryPause=false.
Start and resume both post startSession with the existing mutation key, wait for the Operation and reconcile running state under one lifecycle deadline.
Stop posts stopSession with a mutation key and reconciles stopped state after its Operation; timeout retains local recovery evidence.
An in-process exec cancellation aborts event collection and posts cancelExecution; durable mappings additionally observe a terminal state for up to 30 seconds.
Submit a shell string or shell-quoted argv via createExecution; clamp the rounded timeout to 1–3600 seconds, persist lastExecutionId and start event collection.
Embedded preview create clamps TTL to 60–86400 seconds and validates the returned URL protocol and absence of credentials. No CLI command invokes previews.
Embedded preview revoke requires a URL recorded in this provider instance; after deletePreview returns 200/202, remove its local URL mapping. No CLI command invokes this port.
Legacy push lists receipt pages (limit 100, maximum 100 pages), rejects repeated cursors and uses the latest verified receipt to derive replay lineage.

Legacy push announces content hash, total bytes, chunk count and an identity derived from source plus predecessor receipt; a verified matching receipt avoids repeat upload. Failed status becomes a typed error.
Legacy push checks each local chunk hash and uploads with stable keys; at most 3 retryable attempts, with 409 accepted only for a matching chunk checksum.
Legacy verification may return an apply Operation: poll every 1 second when healthy, then re-verify matching manifest ID, checksum and chunk count before success.

journeys.name: Install the Claude Code adapter
journeys.summary: ocbox agent setup claude-code adds one PreToolUse hook and one allow rule to a Claude Code settings file, with a backup and an ownership manifest.

steps.story: `claude --version` runs with a 15 s limit and must read 2.0.51, the one pinned version; any other output fails with a remediation before a file is read. --claude-version works only when OCBOX_TEST_MODE=1.

It reads managed, local, project and user settings by precedence. An unreadable source, a managed hook lock, or a deny/ask rule overlapping Bash(ocbox exec:*) stops setup with an error and nothing is written.

The target (project scope by default) must stay inside its .claude folder. The merge adds one PreToolUse/Bash hook `ocbox agent hook claude-code --session <id>` with timeout 600 s and the allow rule Bash(ocbox exec:*); other settings survive.

The original file is copied to a timestamped .ocbox-backup-*.json, the settings are written atomically, then ocbox-claude-code-manifest.json (hashes, backup path, created containers). If a write fails the target is restored; a second run reports already-applied.

journeys.name: Install the Codex adapter
journeys.summary: ocbox agent setup codex plans, and with --yes writes, one PreToolUse hook into Codex config.toml or hooks.json, with backups and a per-layer ownership manifest.

steps.story: `codex --version` runs with a 15 s limit and must read the pinned 0.153.4. config.toml and hooks.json under CODEX_HOME (default ~/.codex) or the project .codex folder are parsed; an unknown hooks table is refused with CODEX_SCHEMA_UNSUPPORTED.

For --layer project the repository must be trusted in the user config.toml or the plan is blocked. A Session is required too: --session or the active Session in the lifecycle file; without one the plan reports an error and exits 2.

planCodexSetup builds the hook fragment (id ocbox-codex-<hash>) for PreToolUse/Bash with timeout 600 s, edits config.toml without touching comments (or writes hooks.json), and runs the offline contract proof. Without --yes it only prints the plan.

With --yes each file is backed up as <file>.<time>.ocbox-backup, written atomically, and the manifest saved. If any write fails every written file is restored; if that restore also fails CODEX_ROLLBACK_FAILED points at the backups.

journeys.name: A Codex command runs in the box
journeys.summary: A Codex Bash call is denied locally and run in the selected Session instead, through the owned PreToolUse hook.

steps.story: Codex starts `ocbox agent hook codex --session <id>` for each PreToolUse event and pipes JSON on stdin. A payload that is not valid JSON, has an unknown event or lacks tool_name prints a deny decision and exits 2, so the call is blocked.

Only Bash routes. Other tools, other events, nested calls (OCBOX_CODEX_ADAPTER_ACTIVE=1) and exact owned ocbox commands stay local; Bash with no Session is blocked. A routed call becomes exec --timeout 570000 -- /bin/bash -lc <command>.

The hook runs the normal `ocbox exec` flow with its output sent to stderr: the Session must be active with a running Sandbox. The 570 s remote deadline sits inside the 600 s hook timeout, leaving a 30 s margin for the decision.

After the remote run the hook prints a PreToolUse deny on stdout and exits 0, whatever the remote exit code, so Codex does not run the command a second time. If the routed exec throws, the hook denies with exit 2.

on_failure.story: Any unexpected error while reading stdin or running the hook is redacted and turned into a deny with exit 2 (fail closed), never into exit 1.

journeys.name: Pull workspace changes to the local folder
journeys.summary: ocbox sync pull applies Session-workspace-only changes to the local folder (fake provider only), with a transfer journal and a verified baseline.

steps.story: The command resolves the selected Session, the local folder (default: current directory) and the remote workspace under the state directory. For the hosted ocbox provider pull is refused with CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED before any scan.

Under a per-Session lock (5 s wait, then OPERATION_CONFLICT) it refuses an unresolved transfer journal, scans both sides with the built-in exclusions plus .gitignore, .opencloudboxignore and flags, and plans against the last verified baseline. A conflict stops the pull.

Deletions need --delete plus --yes or a typed y (a terminal without --json/--jsonl). The intent is saved as pending-baseline.json before the local folder changes; excluded local files (secrets, caches) are carried over so a pull never deletes them.

Entries are copied from an archive into a prepared folder and swapped in with a journal (target-moving, target-moved, committed). The pending baseline is promoted only after the commit; if the copy or the swap fails it is rolled back and the old baseline stays.

on_failure.story: A crash leaves a journal. The next sync refuses with RECOVERY_REQUIRED until `ocbox sync recover` restores the original target and reconciles the pending baseline.

journeys.name: Load and validate project configuration
journeys.summary: Every project command first reads opencloudbox.toml, validates it strictly and resolves the state directory and requested resources.

steps.story: The file is opencloudbox.toml in the working directory or --config. A missing file gives CONFIG_INVALID "run ocbox init"; a file over 1 MiB, invalid TOML, or one of nine renamed legacy fields fails with the path and the new name.

The strict schema rejects unknown keys (with a did-you-mean hint). Restricted egress needs 1 to 256 unique hosts, auto-destroy must come after auto-stop, and [env] values may not look like credentials. Messages name paths, never values.

Settings with several sources resolve as flag, then environment, then file, then default. The state directory follows --state-dir, OCBOX_STATE_DIR, then the OS default; a bad environment value is reported by variable name only.

The file becomes a provider-neutral sandbox spec. For the hosted provider only fields present in the file (cpu in cores = millicores / 1000, memory in bytes, image, region, runtime) are sent as a request, and CLI flags override them.

journeys.name: Inspect providers
journeys.summary: ocbox providers lists the registered providers with availability, authentication need and capabilities.

steps.story: Load opencloudbox.toml and resolve the state directory; register fake for local validation and ocbox for hosted API access. Factory creation is deferred until resolution or diagnostics.

Each provider is built and asked for its capabilities. The hosted one advertises streaming, cancellable execution, no memory pause, no file API, authenticated previews and 1 Sandbox per Session; building it needs a hosted project id or it is reported unavailable.

on_failure.story: A provider whose factory throws is listed with available=false and error code PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE; the command itself still succeeds.

steps.story: The result names the configured provider and one row per provider (name, availability, auth, capabilities). Human output prints one line per provider; --json keeps the capability object.

journeys.name: Protect stored sign-in credentials
journeys.summary: How login tokens are written to and read from disk: a protected file, verified owner-only before and after every write.

steps.story: No OS keychain adapter is wired, so tokens go to a file in the platform credential folder. On a WSL /mnt drive there is no safe folder and login fails with CONFIG_INVALID instead of writing there.

A write opens the temp file 0600 and verifies owner-only access (folder 0700; ACL check through PowerShell on Windows) before any token byte is written, then renames and verifies again. A failed check removes the file (CredentialProtectionError).

on_failure.story: If protection cannot be proved after the rename, the committed file is deleted and the error is raised, so a readable token is never left behind.

steps.story: A read fails closed when folder or file protection cannot be proved, and refuses symlinks; a wrong key or invalid JSON is a corruption error (CredentialFileCorruptionError). Non-secret facts live separately in auth.json, which refuses secret-looking content.

journeys.name: Update local Session state safely
journeys.summary: How the CLI changes its own state files: a lock, a validated read, and an atomic replace, so a crash leaves the old or the new file.

steps.story: A change to local state (selected Session, Operations, hosted mappings) takes <file>.lock. It waits 5 s, polls every 25 ms, and takes over a lock older than 30 s whose process is gone. A timeout throws a conflict error instead of writing unlocked.

The lifecycle file is <state>/lifecycle/<project id>.json, the id derived from the working-directory path. Reads and writes are checked against a strict schema; an invalid file fails the command instead of being treated as empty.

The write goes to a 0600 temp file, is fsynced and renamed over the file (Windows retries up to 100 times if a reader holds it), then the folder is fsynced. A crash leaves the old or the new file, never half of each.

Other local files follow the same pattern: hosted sandbox mappings inside the lifecycle file (scoped to the login and project), auth.json for sign-in facts, ocbox-operation-checkpoints.json for the state of each polled Operation. Sync baselines under sync/ use their own atomic writer.

journeys.name: Resume waiting for a hosted operation
journeys.summary: A restarted CLI continues polling a hosted operation from its saved checkpoint instead of starting over.

steps.story: After every poll the CLI saves the Operation state, progress and attempt to ocbox-operation-checkpoints.json. After a restart a terminal checkpoint is returned with no network call; a failed or cancelled one still throws its typed error.

A non-terminal checkpoint continues from its attempt count. The delay is the server Retry-After, else 250 ms doubling to 30 s with up to 20% jitter. The default deadline is 5 min, then OPERATION_TIMEOUT; the operation is not assumed cancelled.
Command output has its own deadline: the requested timeout, else the provider maximum of 3 600 000 ms, else 5 min, plus 30 s of grace, so a long command is not cut off while it is still running.

journeys.name: Choose how command output is reported
journeys.summary: How ocbox exec parses its flags, checks the target, prints output as human text, one JSON result or JSON lines, and picks an exit code.

steps.story: `ocbox exec` accepts --session, --cwd (absolute sandbox path), --timeout (1 to 2147483647 ms), --env NAME=VALUE (credential-looking values refused), --json or --jsonl, then `--` argv or --shell. An unknown option fails before anything starts.

Require an active Session, running primary Sandbox, streaming/cancellation support and a timeout within provider limits. --shell rejects a known non-Linux OS; unknown effective metadata is deferred to the remote executor.

Human mode streams stdout and stderr as they arrive, --jsonl prints one base64 event per line, --json prints a single envelope at the end with up to 64 KiB per stream. Events must arrive in order from sequence 0 with one completed event, or the run fails.

Exit codes: the remote command's own code, 124 on timeout, 125 for an infrastructure failure, 130 when cancelled. The first Ctrl-C asks the provider to cancel; a second one exits at once as cancelled.

journeys.name: Report an error without leaking secrets
journeys.summary: A failing command prints a typed, redacted error: no tokens, command output or host paths reach the terminal or JSON.

steps.story: A failing command prints the error and sets exit code 1. OcboxError carries code, retryable flag (from a 32-code registry), request id and details; details with secret-looking keys, host paths or raw errors are rejected when the error is created.

Output goes through redactForOutput: secret-like keys, stdout/stderr/argv fields and token-shaped strings become [REDACTED], host paths become [LOCAL_PATH]. Human errors go to stderr; --json is indented, --jsonl one envelope (schemaVersion 1) per line.

API failures are mapped from the HTTP status and the public error envelope to a stable code; raw response bytes and headers are never forwarded, and the one-line diagnostic shows only operation, status and request id.

journeys.name: Try the CLI offline with the fake provider
journeys.summary: Without a login, ocbox init selects the fake provider, which keeps sandboxes in a local file and runs commands as host processes for validation.

steps.story: `ocbox init` without a login writes the starter opencloudbox.toml (provider fake: 1 CPU, 2 GiB memory, 10 GiB disk, idle timeout 15 min, maximum runtime 2 h) with mode 0600, creating it exclusively; an existing file is only edited to add flags. After login it defaults to the hosted provider.

The fake provider keeps its resources in <state>/providers/fake.json. Create is idempotent by key and by Session/Operation, so a retry adopts the existing sandbox; a configured fault can drop the first create response (PROVIDER_TIMEOUT).

Commands run through the fake provider execute as a local process on this machine through the helper, with a bounded event queue (capacity 8). It is a contract-test harness for the exec flow, not isolation.

Start/resume/pause/stop/destroy mutate local fake state under its JSON store lock and replay the same idempotency key. Deleted resources reject later non-destroy mutations; injected lost replies retain the recorded effect.

journeys.name: Hosted start is refused by plan limits
journeys.summary: When the hosted service denies a create, the CLI shows a plain message and a typed error, and records the failure locally.

steps.story: createSession sends only the resources named in the config or flags, with the stored idempotency key. A response with status 400 or above is checked for an admission denial code before the generic error mapping.

A denial code (HTTP status 400 or above) is mapped: spec_not_allowed to INVALID_SPEC, admission_closed to PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE, user_active_limit to USAGE_LIMIT, global_capacity to PROVIDER_CAPACITY, budget_exhausted to INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS, each with a plain message.

The lifecycle then records the failure: the create Operation becomes failed and the Session moves to error. A timeout or cancel is treated as ambiguous and keeps the Session in creating so the same create can be resumed.

on_failure.story: A retry reuses the stored idempotency key create:<session>:<operation>, so a lost response cannot create a second hosted sandbox.

journeys.name: Push content-addressed source with resume
journeys.summary: Mapped sesdo_ Sessions use paged source plans, bounded capability uploads and terminal apply receipts; unsigned local checkpoints support retries.

steps.story: Resolve the owned running hosted Session. sesdo_ selects v2; older hosted Sessions keep the legacy push journey. Missing or foreign mappings fail before source upload.

Under the Session lock, scan with CLI ignore rules and immutable state/cache exclusions. Reject unsafe content, collisions, files over 256 MiB or content over 1 GiB; snapshot construction also caps files plus directories at 100000.

Validate unsigned pages and cached bytes. Reuse unchanged slices, otherwise pack 8 MiB bundles or 16 MiB parts; previous state with at most 512 dirty files selects standalone small blobs. Pages are capped at 512 entries/512 KiB.
Require --delete plus confirmation/--yes for locally recorded removed paths. Save unsigned pending pages; reuse an interrupted identity only when pages match and it is younger than 45 minutes.
Send each canonical page with a stable idempotency key. Validate the matching plan and every missing blob against that page; never save returned PUT capability URLs.
Consume opaque PUT capabilities returned by plan with 4 parallel uploads, 120-second attempt timeouts and at most 3 attempts. Never add the API bearer or follow redirects.

on_failure.story: Interruption retains unsigned pending metadata. Rerun push to rehash current source, re-plan missing blobs and continue without persisting capabilities.

steps.story: Replay the same apply key at 1-second intervals while receipts are pending; check a 15-minute loop deadline before calls. Each authenticated control request has its own HTTP/body timers. Only matching succeeded receipts finish.

on_failure.story: Terminal plan refusal clears its pending identity. Other interrupted outcomes remain resumable; errors exit 1 and expose only safe categories.

steps.story: Atomically save success metadata and clear pending state. JSONL emits sync.progress phase/count events then sync.pushed with protocolVersion 2 and uploaded blob/byte counts.

journeys.name: Push into the fake Session workspace
journeys.summary: Fake-provider push uses three-way planning, deletion approval and a journalled local directory swap; hosted pushes use the legacy or CAS journeys instead.

steps.story: Resolve the selected Session and local source/remote workspace. Under the per-Session sync lock, require a safe target, refuse unresolved journals and reconcile any pending baseline intent.
Scan both sides and compare to the verified baseline. Unsafe paths, collisions and concurrent edits fail before the target changes; an empty plan returns applied=false.
For planned deletions require --delete and --yes or interactive y. Save pending-baseline.json before mutation; carry over excluded target paths so secret/cache exclusions survive the replacement.
Stream the desired source through OCBOXA1 into a staged directory, journal the old-target/backup swap, commit and promote the pending baseline only after success.

on_failure.story: Roll back the transaction after a transfer error. Preserve unresolved journal evidence; a baseline write failure reports SYNC_INTEGRITY so recover can compare the installed snapshot.
